# Routing work between Claude and Codex

The goal is to spread token use across both tools while keeping each phase correct. Send work to whichever finishes it with less total effort.

## Choosing the executor

`kit-plan` sets the `Executor` column for every phase. Default to `codex`. Choose `claude` when:

- the phase is small: configuration, documentation, wiring, or a few lines across files;
- it depends on judgment the prompt cannot carry well, such as subtle design trade-offs, API compatibility decisions, or matching an unusual local convention;
- it mostly edits plan, workflow or agent instruction files.

The user can change any executor at Gate 1. With `--claude-only`, or when Codex is unavailable, every phase is `claude`.

## Fix rounds

Before each round, classify the failures from `kit-test`:

| Pick Claude (`kit-fix`) when all of these hold | Pick Codex (`codex exec resume`) when any of these holds |
|---|---|
| About 3 or fewer distinct root causes (count causes, not failing tests: one bug can fail many tests) | Many independent root causes, or failures spread across several modules |
| The cause is clear and local: typo, import, edge case, type or lint error, wrong constant | The implementation misread the requirement or misses a feature |
| The fix touches a few lines in files you already know | The fix means rewriting or restructuring a large part of the phase |
| Codex has already failed this exact issue once | Most of the phase has to be reimplemented |

If Codex is unavailable, Claude handles every round.

A phase Claude implemented is fixed by Claude. Hand it to Codex only for a large rework, and only through a fresh `codex exec` with the implement prompt plus the failure evidence, because there is no session to resume.

## Budget

- At most 3 fix rounds per phase, counting Claude and Codex rounds together. Record the count in `plan.md`.
- A Codex retry after an unknown infrastructure failure does not count. A Codex run that returns a result does count.
- When the third round still fails, set the phase to `blocked` and stop. Report the failing commands with their real output, what each round tried, and a suggested next step.

## User rejection

A rejection at Gate 2 starts a new cycle with a fresh 3-round budget (0 of 3 used). Route the user's feedback with the same table as test failures. Feedback that changes requirements goes to Codex (`codex exec resume`, feedback verbatim) when Codex implemented the phase. Everything else goes to Claude: a new `revise` [phase worker](phase-worker.md) receives the feedback verbatim. The coordinator never applies the feedback itself.
